Subject: Post-demo: Redwood Inference — buying committee recap & next steps

Hi Sofia, Priya, Michael —

Thanks again for taking the time today to run through Redwood Inference with the Acme buying committee. I appreciate the candid feedback and the clear decision criteria you shared. Quick recap and agreed next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Attendees (Acme): Sofia Martinez (Head of Product / economic sponsor), Michael Chen (InfoSec lead), Priya Singh (Legal), James O'Neill (Procurement, joined for last 10 mins)
Redwood team: Marissa Cole (AE), Vivek Kulkarni (SE), Aditya Rao (Sales Manager), Lauren Bishop (Customer Success), Neha Kapoor (Legal Ops)

Key decision criteria highlighted by the committee:
- Security & compliance: SOC 2, data residency controls, SSO / SCIM, key management
- Cost predictability: unit economics, reserved capacity options
- Reliability & fallbacks: SLA for latency and uptime, multi-region options
- Integrations & rollout: API support for streaming, prefix caching, and SDKs for product embedding

Agreed next steps (owners & timelines):
1) Security package & evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test summary, data flow diagram) — Redwood to share by Fri 2/20 — Owner: Neha Kapoor (redwood) / Action: Michael to confirm any additional artifacts needed
2) Technical deep-dive for engineering (latency, KV caching, auth) — schedule a 60m session week of 2/23 — Owner: Vivek Kulkarni (redwood) / Action: Michael & Sofia to share preferred times
3) Commercial proposal + sample SOW & SLA — Redwood to send initial proposal by Fri 2/20 — Owner: Marissa Cole (redwood) / Action: James to confirm procurement info (billing entity, PO process)
4) Legal intake (standard DPA + any bespoke clauses) — Redwood legal to review and flag likely redlines within 5 business days after proposal — Owner: Neha Kapoor / Action: Priya to provide priority clauses if any
5) Decision window — Acme indicated target for vendor selection by end of March; we penciled in an exec review week of 3/22

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-Acme-20260218.pdf (initial commercial ask), SLA-FAQ.pdf

Would you like us to prioritize anything differently? If not, we'll proceed to compile the security package and commercial proposal and follow up with proposed slots for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great demo. A couple quick clarifying Qs from InfoSec before we schedule the deep-dive:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key)?
- Data residency: can we restrict inference processing to us-west-2?
- SSO: do you support SAML + SCIM provisioning out of the box?

Also, can you include any retention/default delete policies for cached prompts / KV stores? Procurement copied to loop them in early.

—Michael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood Inference — buying committee recap & next steps

Hi Michael — thanks, great questions. Short answers here and we'll include formal artifacts in the security package by Fri: 
- KMS: Yes — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS for our Private and Dedicated deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can discuss BYOK for enterprise plans. Owner: Neha will attach the KMS integration summary.
- Data residency: We can route and pin inference workloads to us-west-2 in Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can select region with reserved capacity commitments. We'll include regional routing docs.
- SSO / SCIM: SAML SSO supported today; SCIM provisioning available for Dedicated and Private (hosting roadmap for hosted tier).
- Retention: By default, short-term KV/prefix caches are ephemeral; persistent logs/trace for debugging are configurable — we'll include default retention windows and options for reduced retention or deletion-on-demand.

Action items updated: Neha will attach SOC 2 scope + pen test summary; Vivek will prepare a 60m technical deep-dive agenda; Marissa will circulate commercial proposal and sample SOW.

If helpful, I've included a suggested owner mapping for Acme to make approvals efficient:
- Economic buyer / product sponsor: Sofia Martinez
- InfoSec / security reviewer: Michael Chen
- Legal reviewer: Priya Singh
- Procurement / contracting: James O'Neill (procurement@acmecorp.com)

We should know by Fri if any additional artifacts are required.

Best,
Marissa
